summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied under F. E. L. Priestley and earned his doctorate under Anthony Kennedy Warder, holding an attested post at the University of Toronto in 1991.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. (~1976–1979) and D.Phil. (~1979–1983) from the University of Hamburg. He served at the University of Washington (attested 1989–1996) and became a Harvard professor in 1995.

Leopold von Schroeder (1851–1920) was an Indologist who studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Leipzig, Jena, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu (~1882–1894), the University of Innsbruck (~1896–1899), and the University of Vienna (~1899–1920).

Leslie S. Kawamura (1935–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD under Herbert V. Guenther at the University of Saskatchewan (~1971–1975) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary from ~1976 to 2010.

Levi McLaughlin works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University (PhD 2009), his career includes posts at Kokugakuin University, Wofford College, National University of Singapore, University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University.

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London and has held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson (~1963–1968). He held a long career at the University of California, Berkeley, serving from ~1967 and becoming professor emeritus in ~2002.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991) and secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000). In 2000, he became Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center.
Liang Cai works in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held an appointment as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).
Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and completed her PhD at SOAS University of London.
Lin Heng is an Indology scholar who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).

Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).

Linda Learman specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral work under Robert P. Weller and undertook postdoctoral mentorship under Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).
Linda Penkower works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She was a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983) and earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993.
Lindsay G. McCune works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan, completing an MA under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2007).
Ling Ji is a sinology scholar who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo (attested 2014).

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist educated at the University of Liverpool and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held positions at the British Museum, University College London (~1906–1917), and SOAS University of London (~1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He has held academic posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. During his career, he held posts at West China Union University, the Ethnic Publishing House, and the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China.
